summary: Claude Code responded to the plain checkbox request by reading index.html and editing it directly, adding `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">` in about 16 seconds. No brainstorming skill, no clarifying questions, no go-ahead request.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied per the session log (ground truth) and the resulting file on disk. The only oddity is the missing token-usage artifact, reported as an observation.

observations.description: Post-edit message offers optional follow-ups (persistence, strikethrough, localStorage) without blocking — appropriate, but worth noting it does volunteer extra scope suggestions.

The scenario references a cost artifact `coding-agent-token-usage.json`, but `find` over the run results directory returned no such file at the time the session ended, so the headline token total was not observable to me.

Launching required stepping through four onboarding/consent screens (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) with defaults set to "No, exit" — easy to accidentally quit the run.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence was only: Bash(`ls -la && git status --short`), Read(index.html), Edit(index.html old_string `    <main></main>`). index.html on disk now contains `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">`. Screen: "Sautéed for 16s · done 2:06 AM".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: `grep -o 'superpowers:brainstorming' .../projects/*/*.jsonl | wc -l` returned 0; jq over tool_use entries showed no Skill invocation at all (only Bash/Read/Edit). Final reply asked nothing before editing: "Added a native checkbox to index.html:9 ... Nothing was committed. If you later want the state persisted ... say the word."
